title: Prepare() treats worktree as ready from .git dir existence alone
body:
## Problem

`Manager.Prepare` in `internal/worktree/worktree.go:76-79` decides whether a task worktree is already fully prepared solely by checking that a `.git` directory exists:

```go
// Already prepared (daemon cloned before container acquire).
if st, statErr := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, ".git")); statErr == nil && st.IsDir() {
    return dir, branch, nil
}
```

`git clone` creates the `.git` directory early in the clone process, before the checkout of the working tree completes, and well before the subsequent `checkout -b archie/issue-N` step (worktree.go:93) runs. If `archied` is killed or restarted (OOM, deploy, crash) while a clone is in progress, on the next start `Prepare()` will see the existing `.git` directory and short-circuit, assuming the worktree is fully set up  --  skipping the clone, the `checkout -b` branch creation, and any config steps.

## Why it matters

This directly conflicts with the package's stated goal of being safely restartable: the package doc for `internal/daemon/daemon.go:3` states "the daemon is restartable ... at any point." With this shortcut, a restart mid-clone leaves a `.git` directory but an incomplete/missing working tree and no `archie/issue-N` branch. Later calls to `CommitAll` (git add/status/commit) or `Push` (git push -u origin branch) will then operate on this broken state  --  failing with confusing errors, or in the worst case running against whatever branch actually exists (e.g. the base branch) rather than the intended `archie/issue-N` branch.

## Suggested fix

Strengthen the "already prepared" check to verify actual completion, not just `.git` existence, e.g.:
- Confirm the target branch exists and is checked out (`git rev-parse --verify <branch>` / check `HEAD`), and
- Confirm the working tree is non-empty / clone actually finished (e.g. check for a marker file written only after the full clone+checkout sequence succeeds, or verify `git status` runs without error and matches expected branch).

A simple robust option: write a sentinel file (e.g. `.archie-prepared`) as the very last step of the success path, and gate the early-return solely on that sentinel rather than on `.git` alone.
</refined_body>
